project.title: Cairn
project.pitch: Cairn is an open-source Telegram bot for Starknet that anyone can host. It answers balance and transaction lookups in chat, alerts you when a watched wallet moves funds or grants an approval, posts a project group's token buys and whale moves with USD values and .stark names, and warns everyone when the chain stalls or reorganises. It only reads the chain, over any JSON-RPC 0.10 node: it never holds a key, never signs, has no Mini App, and runs as one Node.js 24 process with no dependencies.

rounds.title: Lookups
criteria: Usefulness of replies (counts double): /status, /balance and /tx tell a Starknet user what they need at a glance, with exact amounts and working links, in a private chat and in a busy group
Robustness: every bad input, flaky node and Telegram error gets a reason a user or an operator can act on, and nothing crashes
Security posture: secrets, hosts and data are handled as the brief says, including where the checks cannot see
Code quality: small, readable modules with no dependency, ready for round 2's block scanner and delivery ledger

rounds.title: Wallet alerts
criteria: Alert quality (counts double): an alert says what moved, how much, between whom and where to check; no dust or fee noise, and a busy wallet does not bury the reader
Delivery correctness: no lost alerts and no duplicates, through restarts, kills, node outages and paging
Admin control and privacy: group setup is obvious and members cannot change it; only what the brief allows is stored; /export is complete and /forget leaves nothing
Code quality: round 1 reused, not copied, with a scanner and a ledger ready for round 3's swap decoders

rounds.title: Group feeds, prices and names
criteria: Group fit (counts double): a post reads at a glance on a phone, scales with trade size, and bursts never flood the group
Decoding accuracy: buys, sells, aggregator routes, multi-hop routes and round trips are counted as the brief defines, and amounts and USD values match the chain
Names and prices: they appear where they help, are never wrong, and stay quiet when unknown
Code quality: the decoders sit on round 2's scanner and ledger

rounds.title: Network guard and operations
criteria: Trustworthiness under failure (counts double): stalls, reorgs and dead endpoints are each reported once and accurately, and alerts are corrected when the chain changes its mind
Operability: health, metrics, failover and the deploy guide let a community member run it unattended
Member safety: the guards catch seed phrases and listed links with no false alarms, and never repeat what they protect
Code quality: earlier rounds reused; one loop, not four
